# MCP compatibility fixtures

The context cases specify the existing Gateway ingress classifications, including raw unknown declarations, mismatched/invalid declarations with no effective version, discovery, subscription and signed errors. They are persistence inputs, not an assertion that every producer accepts every protocol request.

The legacy JSON, BSON and wire fixtures are independently specified old shapes. They contain API/organization identity and the original four MCP fields; the protobuf fixture also includes the old producer’s always-emitted zero-valued Geo (with all three submessages), Latency and Network messages, plus epoch timestamps and UTC timezone. They are not generated by encoding the current Go record with zero-valued new fields. BSON uses historical lowercase `jsonrpcmethod`; MCP record JSON uses `JSONRPCMethod`; SQL retains `jsonrpc_method`.

The hex files are fixed bytes: BSON string elements; MessagePack maps keyed by the historical exported Go field names; protobuf AnalyticsRecord fields16(APIID),17(OrgID),33(MCPStats), with nested fields1(IsMCP),2(method),3(primitive type),4(name). Its other old fields are13/28(epoch timestamps),19(Latency),23(Geo),24(Network),30(UTC timezone). None contains new protobuf fields5–8 or new protocol/error record fields. Tests decode these unchanged bytes and assert both surviving legacy values and zero defaults.

`mcp_signed_codes/` contains eight separate complete synthetic AnalyticsRecord
JSON inputs. Their integers are literal signed boundary values; tests use typed
integers or json.Number, never an untyped float64 roundtrip. API/key data is
synthetic and `api_key` is absent. Runtime queue-injection QA substitutes only the
explicit API identity and User-Agent run-marker placeholders and retains exact
input/effective/encoded hashes. These direct producer cases complement actual
Gateway/mock requests and must not be described as upstream MCP calls.

`mcp_int32_977/` freezes the complete protobuf source from
977a5ddcda4a523337b4d8e8dd36a0df03c81aef and its descriptor compiled by protoc
3.21.12. `provenance.json` records source and descriptor hashes. It independently
models that candidate's int32 field8 reader, separate from the pre-context
fields1–4 fixtures. Signed32 wire bytes remain identical; its documented
truncation of wider values is a compatibility limitation, not a passing wide-code
interoperability claim. The current int64 descriptor is not used to derive this
old shape.
